test_title: SSC Stenographer 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 12 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Salman finishes the work / within hours but he / delays it if not / accompanying by Rohit.
solution:
The correct answer is '**accompanying by Rohit**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The segment "**accompanying by Rohit**" contains a grammatical mistake in the form of a passive voice construction error.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**accompanied by Rohit**" to correctly use the passive voice form.
 
• The passive voice construction in this context requires the past participle form of the verb "**accompany**," which is "**accompanied**," rather than the present participle form "**accompanying**."
 
• The correction ensures that the sentence accurately describes the condition under which Salman delays his work, emphasizing that the delay occurs when he is not accompanied by Rohit.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

**Correct Sentence:** *Salman finishes the work within hours but he delays it if not **accompanied by Rohit***.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**within hours but he**" is grammatically correct and effectively joins the two parts of the sentence, indicating the contrast between the time Salman takes to finish work and his behavior under certain conditions.
 
• "**Salman finishes the work**" is a correctly formed segment that subject-verb-object structure to introduce the subject and action.
 
• "**delays it if not**" is also grammatically correct, beginning the clause that details the condition under which Salman delays his work, but it relies on the final segment to complete the condition.
